question: When the AbortSignal is already aborted, does each adapter fail before any request leaves the process with an identifiable abort error, and when a stream is aborted mid-flight does iteration terminate promptly with a clear error?
finding: Pre-dispatch (signal already aborted): @google/genai threw nothing (returned) (abort-distinguishable=false, HTTP none, requests that left the process: yes); the AI SDK threw AbortError (abort-distinguishable=true, HTTP none, requests that left the process: no). Mid-stream: genai saw 1 chunk(s) and threw AbortError in 0ms; the AI SDK saw 3 chunk(s) and threw AbortError in 0ms. The AI SDK short-circuits an already-aborted signal on its own (fetch level), so llxprt's throwIfAborted guard would be redundant on that path; @google/genai only registers an abort listener and lets the call through, which is exactly why that guard exists today.
